lesson_title: Same R400, Three Prices: R2 vs R7,30 vs R60
hook_text: Withdrawing R400 can cost R2... or R60. Same money. Different door.
clip_script: Follow one R400 note out of the account by three different doors. Door one, the supermarket till: ask for cashback, pay R2,00. Door two, the bank's ATM: R2,50 plus R1,20 per hundred — R7,30, more than three times the till. Door three, the branch counter: R60,00 — thirty times the till price for the identical notes. Now run the year. Weekly cash at the till: R104 for the year. Weekly cash at the counter: R3 120. The difference could buy a car wash a new pressure washer. Same money, same year — the only variable was which door you made a habit of. Nobody loses their savings to one giant fee. They lose them R7,30 at a time, without watching.
visual_style: Three doors side by side with price tags; a R400 note walks through each, shedding coins — tiny at door one, a shower of notes at door three; year totals stack into two towers.
pacing: Three quick door reveals, then the slow shocking year comparison.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to pick the right account and dodge the fee traps.
